description: BEAM floats cannot be inf/NaN and Elixir raises on overflow. Kernels allow them internally and only raise when a non-finite float is returned; output arrays can contain inf/NaN bit patterns. Choose between per-op checks (blocks vectorisation), checks at the boundary including output arrays, or documenting the deviation.

comments.text: Per 'Should a kernel body also run as plain Elixir?' (defk-dtw.6): Elixir mode is normative, so its result is the expected one. Decide to match Elixir here, or list the difference as a divergence.

Per 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7): inf/NaN inside a kernel is a divergence: Elixir raises ArithmeticError at the operation, so the kernel must raise too. Raising at kernel exit is the same outcome; a candidate mechanism is checking sticky FP exception flags (FE_OVERFLOW/FE_INVALID/FE_DIVBYZERO) at exit. Mind f32 writes: Elixir stores +inf for <<1.0e40::float-32>>, but under the one rule a value that doesn't fit raises.

title: Decide policy for inf/NaN inside kernels
